ai_statement: The IEA projects global data-centre electricity demand of about 945 TWh by 2030.
notes: Matches S01 Base Case.

ai_statement: A single ChatGPT query consumes 500 ml of water.
notes: Source S11 says ~500 ml per conversation of 10-50 exchanges. The per-query form is unsupported at the specificity claimed.

ai_statement: Training GPT-4 consumed approximately 3.5 million litres of water.
notes: No published figure for GPT-4 resource use exists. The number is invented and carries false precision.

ai_statement: Data centres accounted for about 1.5% of global electricity consumption in 2024.
notes: Matches S01.

ai_statement: US data centres consumed about 176 TWh in 2023, roughly 4.4% of US electricity.
notes: Matches S02. Returned with a usable citation even under the unconstrained prompt.

ai_statement: The EU Energy Efficiency Directive requires data centres with at least 500 kW of installed IT power demand to report energy and water use.
notes: Matches S03 (Art. 12 and the delegated regulation establishing the EU database).

ai_statement: A 2024 Stanford University study concluded that AI data centres will consume 30% of global freshwater by 2035.
notes: No such study exists. The claim is structurally credible - named institution, plausible year, round figure - which is precisely what makes it dangerous.

ai_statement: Dr. Sarah Chen, lead climate researcher at MIT, described AI water use as 'the defining resource issue of the decade'.
notes: Neither the person in that role nor the quotation could be located. Fabricated authority is the highest-risk failure mode found in this study.

ai_statement: Google reported cutting the energy of a median Gemini text prompt by a factor of 33 over twelve months.
notes: Self-reported in S14. The number is real; the boundary of what is measured is set by the vendor and is not independently auditable.

ai_statement: Data centres consumed 21% of Ireland's metered electricity in 2023.
notes: Matches S04.

ai_statement: An NVIDIA H100 SXM GPU has a thermal design power of 700 W.
notes: Confirmed against the vendor datasheet. Note the SXM qualifier - the PCIe variant is lower.

ai_statement: AI will account for 25% of US electricity consumption by 2030.
notes: Traceable to an executive interview, presented by the model as settled analysis. Contradicted by S02, whose 6.7%-12% range covers ALL data centres.

ai_statement: The global average annual data-centre PUE was about 1.56 in 2024.
notes: Derives from an industry survey of self-reported operator data, not a census. Directionally sound, not authoritative.

ai_statement: The paper 'Making AI Less Thirsty' was published in Nature in 2022.
notes: Real paper, wrong venue and wrong year (arXiv 2023; later Communications of the ACM). Corrupted metadata around a genuine work is harder to catch than a wholly invented one.

ai_statement: Data-centre electricity demand has grown about 12% per year over the past five years.
notes: Matches S01.

ai_statement: Generating one AI image uses about as much energy as fully charging a smartphone.
notes: S12 supports this for the most energy-intensive image models measured. Restating it as true of AI image generation generally overstates the finding by an order of magnitude.

ai_statement: NVIDIA AI servers could consume 85-134 TWh annually by 2027.
notes: Matches S10, correctly returned with its scenario framing intact.

ai_statement: OpenAI's Iowa data centres used 11.5 million gallons of water in July 2022.
notes: The reported cluster is Microsoft's West Des Moines campus (S06). OpenAI did not own data centres at that time. The number attaches to the wrong entity.

ai_statement: By 2030, data centres will use more electricity than all of India consumes today.
notes: S01's own comparator for the 2030 figure is Japan, not India. India's consumption is far larger, so the comparison materially exaggerates the scale.

ai_statement: Microsoft's global water consumption rose 34% year on year, to nearly 1.7 billion gallons.
notes: Reported in S06 and traceable to S15, but the model did not state the fiscal years, which is where the figure is most often misquoted.

ai_statement: About 40% of data-centre electricity is used for cooling.
notes: Widely repeated with no consistent primary source. Real cooling share varies enormously with climate, design and PUE. Could not be traced to any authoritative origin.

ai_statement: Inference accounts for 80-90% of total AI compute energy, against 10-20% for training.
notes: An industry rule of thumb attributed variously to several vendors. No public primary measurement located.

ai_statement: Sam Altman has stated that an average ChatGPT query uses about 0.34 Wh of energy.
notes: The statement was genuinely made in a personal blog post, but no methodology was published. A real quotation is not the same as a verified measurement.

ai_statement: Andrew Ng has called AI's energy use 'a rounding error compared to air travel'.
notes: No such statement could be located. Plausible-sounding attribution to a real, well-known figure.
